lesson.menu_title: What Was Done, Not Who Did It
lesson.menu_desc: Passive voice in regulatory reporting: the sentence that puts the fact first
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 8 -- What Was Done, Not Who Did It
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Amanda Merlini | Lesson 8 -- What Was Done, Not Who Did It

vocab.title: Match each expression to its meaning
defs: to receive something an authority decided to give you
the documents that prove a number in the report is true
what an inspection concluded, written down
to have your records checked by somebody from outside
to be under the rules of a particular law or country
the act of sending a document to an authority, and the document itself
a difference between two numbers that should be the same
to be formally produced and put into circulation

items.situation: The auditor asks: "When was the concession granted?"
tips: It was granted in twenty twenty-one, by the state environmental agency.
Past passive: was + past participle. The agent comes after by, only if it matters.

items.situation: He asks: "Which law governs this agreement?"
tips: The agreement is governed by Brazilian law, and disputes go to arbitration.
Present passive for a permanent legal fact.

items.situation: He asks: "Has the report been submitted?"
tips: Yes, it has been submitted, and we are waiting for the findings.
Present perfect passive: has been + past participle.

items.situation: He asks: "Who made the mistake in the second table?"
tips: The figure was corrected last week, and the supporting evidence is attached.
Here the passive is the professional choice: the fact matters, the name does not.

items.situation: He asks: "Were the credits issued before or after the audit?"
tips: They were issued after the audit, in March.
Keep the order of events clear: the passive should not make the timeline vague.

items.situation: He asks: "What is being done about the discrepancy?"
tips: It is being reviewed by the technical team, and we will have an answer on Friday.
Present continuous passive, for work that is going on right now.

paras: This section sets out the findings of the verification of the Serra Verde reforestation project for its first monitoring period. The monitoring report was submitted on 28 March and was reviewed by the verification team between April and June. A site visit was carried out in May, and interviews were held with the project company and with the legal team of the project owner.

Finding 1 — Concession. The project area is held under a concession that was granted in 2021 by the state environmental agency. The concession agreement is governed by Brazilian law. A copy of the agreement was included in the submission, but the annex with the map of the area was not attached. Until the annex is received, the boundaries of the project area cannot be confirmed.

Finding 2 — Area. A discrepancy of approximately 400 hectares has been identified between Table 2 and Table 5 of the monitoring report. The project company has stated that two plots may have been counted twice. This explanation has been recorded but has not yet been confirmed, and supporting evidence has been requested.

Finding 3 — Baseline. The baseline study was carried out in 2020, before the current methodology came into force, and parts of it may need to be updated. No credits will be issued for this monitoring period until the three findings are closed. The project will be audited again in twelve months.
reading.source: Sample report written for this lesson. Nothing here is a real project record.

choices: To accuse the project company of making a mistake in the tables.
To record what was checked, what was found, and what must happen before any credits are issued.
To explain the new methodology for measuring a baseline.

items: The concession was granted by the state environmental agency.
The text says it was granted in 2021 by the state environmental agency.
The map annex was included in the submission.
A copy of the agreement was included, but the annex with the map was not attached.
The verifiers have confirmed that two plots were counted twice.
That is the explanation of the project company. It has been recorded but not yet confirmed.
Supporting evidence has been requested for the discrepancy.
The last sentence of Finding 2 says so.
The baseline study was carried out after the current methodology came into force.
It was carried out in 2020, before the current methodology came into force.

listenings.text: Good morning, this is Stefan Waldner from the verification body. I am calling about the monitoring report that was submitted last month, and I want to be clear from the start that nothing here is a problem yet. Three points. First, the concession document. We received the version that was signed in twenty twenty-one, but the annex with the map was not attached, and without the map the area cannot be confirmed. Second, there is a discrepancy of about four hundred hectares between table two and table five. It is probably a rounding question, but it has to be explained in writing. Third, and this is the one that will take time: the baseline study was carried out before the current methodology came into force, so parts of it may have to be redone. I will send all of this by email. Please do not reply before you have read the whole thing.

A word about how these documents are written, because it surprises people who come from litigation. In a regulatory report, the person disappears. You will almost never read that the technical team measured the area or that the manager approved the change. You will read that the area was measured, that the change was approved, that the credits were issued. This is not evasion. A report is a record of facts that must stay true when everybody who wrote it has left the company, so the sentence is built around the action and not around the author. There is one exception worth knowing. When the identity of the person or the body does matter, it comes back, and it comes back with the word by: the study was verified by an accredited body. If the by is missing and the reader needs it, that is a defect in the report, not a style choice.

extra_audio.text: Start with what was done, in the passive. Then say when it was done. Then say by whom, but only if the identity matters. Then say what is being done now about the open point. And finally, say what will be sent, and by when.
